title: Early tunes and jitney dances
summary: His first tunes came from Chris Kelly; description of jitney dance jobs with short choruses.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: What were some of the early tunes that you remember? You know, way back.

Well, my first tune, what I used to play, yes, that's my baby. And then I got saved about Chris. I played the blues by Maryland and Going Back to Jamaica. And mostly everything that Chris played that I knew that the folks was interested and liked it, I built up on that.
Now that Going Back to Jamaica is the same thing as West Indies Blues and all that. That's right.

We'll call it Going Back to Jamaica, yeah. Well that's his to feature himself with that wah-wah. See? He played a tune, open with the horn, but when he gets to his time to feature himself, well that's why he did a lot of that. And that's his main tune and my Maryland.

Well a Jitney dance is where they chose one time as a Nicola to dance, they had girls awake there. Anybody who wanted to come in, most of the sailors and so forth would come in, they'd buy a string of tickets, and we'd play the song very short. In other words, I'd play the first chorus, it depends on the bottom of the song, and Paul would take it out. I'd get ready for the next one to pick up.

Yeah, make them short, then make money. Then we'd have what you call a five minute slow drag or five minutes, well that'd you get a chance to play the music or play something long. Five minute waltz or five minute fox strata, five minutes what's never made be. You see?
Well those girls, did they make out all right with that money? Well I think they got about a half or something. Oh yeah, they made out all right.
Made all right. I waked it there, then I waked at the moonlight up on St. Charles and Paul Jitney. And Paul Jitney upstairs.
That was on the Riverside, downtown side corner on St. Charles Street. Right on the corner was upstairs.
Sam Pichota has that restaurant there, and Curly's or something?

Yeah, the restaurant downstairs at that time. I don't know if it's the same people or what, but Jimmy was operating the dance hall upstairs. Yeah, that's how that went to George. They'd buy a string of tickets.
